item.text: {"analysis_packet":{"certificate":"Contract-first arbitration: preserve online legality, unique currently-cached integer evictions, and byte-capacity safety as hard obligations; among behavioral objectives, prioritize scan resistance, then phase-shift adaptation, and resolve object-hit versus byte-hit conflicts in favor of byte-weighted recurring-value retention while rejecting one-hit scan pollution.","witnesses":["The task requires one-access-at-a-time decisions with no hidden-trace, oracle, or benchmark visibility.","The capacity constraint is expressed in bytes, so byte-weighted retention is the coherent tie-break under object-versus-byte conflict.","The stated bottleneck is anchor-local priority setting; anchor implementation details therefore provide context but not behavioral authority.","Scan resistance and phase adaptation require recurring-use evidence to outweigh isolated recency and stale historical preference."],"obligations":["Emit no policy source or implementation edits.","Keep the disposition qualitative, single, and internally consistent.","Require every eviction to identify a currently cached unique integer key.","Require every resulting state to remain within capacity_bytes and remain online-only.","Use the disposition as priority evidence while leaving construction authority to the terminal constructor."],"exact_actions":["Adopt scan resistance as the primary behavioral priority.","Use phase-shift responsiveness as the secondary priority, allowing stale preference to yield to current recurring-use evidence.","When object hit rate and byte hit rate conflict, prefer byte-weighted recurring value while avoiding retention justified only by a single large-object access.","Treat contract legality and capacity safety as overriding all behavioral preferences.","Pass this disposition unchanged to terminal_policy_constructor."]},"artifact_kind":"analysis_only"}
